title: Persist review state and harden the agent pipeline
description: Umbrella for the next significant changes to loupe after the initial scaffold. The MVP keeps comment submit/resolve state in frontend memory only and has a known agent-console glitch. This epic tracks making review state durable and the agent stream reliable, and is the parent for follow-on work in that area.
acceptance_criteria: Review/comment state survives a page reload; the agent console renders each message exactly once; child issues completed.
close_reason: Superseded: pivoting loupe from a Go web app to a VS Code extension (scorched-earth restart).

title: Persist comment submit/resolve state across reloads
description:
Comment submitted/collapsed/edit state currently lives only in React state (web/src/App.tsx), so a page refresh loses which comments were submitted/resolved. The backend already stores submitted comment rows per review but the frontend never reloads them.

Scope:
- Add a 'resolved' (and/or 'submitted') column to the comments table in internal/store/store.go.
- Add GET endpoints to list reviews and their comments in internal/server/server.go.
- On load, hydrate the frontend comment list (with ids, submitted, collapsed) from the backend instead of starting empty.
- Persist edits/deletes/resolve-toggles back to the server.
acceptance_criteria: After submitting comments and reloading the page, submitted comments reappear collapsed/resolved with correct anchors; pending count and submit gating are preserved; edits and deletes persist.
close_reason: Superseded: pivoting loupe from a Go web app to a VS Code extension (scorched-earth restart).

comments.author: coordinator
comments.text:
Implementation complete: Implemented loupe-1mf.1: persist comment submit/resolve state across reloads.

STORE (internal/store/store.go): added `submitted`/`collapsed` columns to the comments table with idempotent ALTER migrations (handles the pre-existing .loupe/loupe.db); AddComment now returns the new id; added EnsureReview (get-or-create one long-lived review per branch/base pair), Reviews(branch,base) listing, UpdateComment, CommentByID, DeleteComment, MarkSubmitted (flags pending→submitted+collapsed, returns the batch), SetMode, and a scanComments helper.

SERVER (internal/server/server.go): new routes — GET /api/reviews (filter by ?branch&base, comments embedded for one-call hydration), POST /api/reviews (ensure draft, no agent run), GET/POST /api/reviews/{id}/comments, PATCH /api/comments/{id} (partial update via pointer fields), DELETE /api/comments/{id}, POST /api/reviews/{id}/submit (marks the pending batch submitted, then runs the agent on just that batch). runReview refactored to take the submitted batch. WebSocket route unchanged.

FRONTEND (web/src/api.ts, web/src/App.tsx): comment ids are now backend integers; on branch/base load the app calls ensureReview + listReviews and hydrates comments with their submitted/collapsed flags instead of starting empty; create/edit/delete/collapse-toggle/submit all persist to the server.

Quality gates: `go build ./...` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `cd web && npm install && npm run build` succeeds (binary re-embeds web_dist via make build).

Runtime smoke test (API-level, exactly what a browser reload exercises): created review → added comment → submitted → re-fetched: comment reappears with submitted:true, collapsed:true and correct path/line/side anchor. Edits persist (reopen sets submitted:false, body updated). Deletes persist (count 2→1). Empty-pending submit is gated with 400. Submit correctly spawned the claude agent (and used --resume with the stored session_id on the second run). DB restored to its pre-test state afterward; no stray processes left.

Acceptance: 4/4 criteria met. NOT committed — awaiting review approval. Files changed: internal/store/store.go, internal/server/server.go, web/src/api.ts, web/src/App.tsx, internal/server/web_dist/index.html (rebuilt).

title: Fix duplicate final message in agent console
description:
The agent's closing summary renders twice in the browser console. The agent emits its final text as an assistant 'text' event, and the terminal 'result' event carries the same text again; both are pushed to the events list in web/src/App.tsx.

Fix options:
- Stop forwarding result text as displayable content in internal/agent/agent.go (use EventResult only as a done marker), or
- In the frontend, skip rendering a 'result' event whose text duplicates the previous 'text' event.
acceptance_criteria: A completed agent run shows its final summary exactly once in the console.
close_reason: Superseded: pivoting loupe from a Go web app to a VS Code extension (scorched-earth restart).

comments.author: coordinator
comments.text:
Implementation complete: Fixed duplicate final summary in the agent console (loupe-1mf.2).

ROOT CAUSE: claude's stream-json emits the final assistant prose as an `assistant`/`text` line AND repeats it in the terminal `result` line. agent.go forwards both as EventText (agent.go:97) and EventResult (agent.go:104), and the frontend rendered both → summary shown twice.

FIX (frontend layer, web/src/App.tsx ws.onmessage): the `result` event is now rendered only when its trimmed text differs from the preceding event's text (and is non-empty); otherwise it's skipped as a display item while `setRunning(false)` still fires as the done-marker. Chose the frontend over agent.go because the `result` field is sometimes the SOLE carrier of final text (error subtypes, runs ending on tool_use) — dropping it at the source would lose the summary in those cases. This guarantees exactly-once in both the normal (duplicate) and edge (sole-carrier) cases.

VERIFICATION:
- Captured a REAL `claude -p --output-format stream-json` run: confirmed assistant text and result.result are byte-identical ("The summary is done.").
- Replayed that real stream through agent.go's exact transform + the new frontend reducer: summary renders exactly 1 time, running=false fires. PASS.
- Edge cases (sole-carrier, differing result text, empty result) all verified: summary never dropped, no empty noise.
- No regression to loupe-1mf.1 comment hydration (untouched useEffect).

QUALITY GATES: `go build ./...` clean; `go vet ./...` clean; `cd web && npm install && npm run build` succeeds; `make build && ./loupe` boots and serves the SPA (verified /api/branches + SPA title).

Files changed: web/src/App.tsx (1 handler; +11/-1). NOT committed — awaiting review approval.

title: Changeset navigation & uncommitted-change review
description:
Two related improvements to how loupe presents and navigates a changeset:

1. Review uncommitted/working-tree changes (not just committed branch diffs).
2. A collapsible file-tree sidebar on the left for navigating files in a changeset.

Both are mostly frontend with a thin backend slice for the working-tree diff. They share the diff-rendering and review-state code paths in web/src/App.tsx and internal/git. See child issues for detail.
design:
Current state (researched 2026-05-20):
- git.Diff runs 'git diff <merge-base(base,branch)> <branch>' — commit-to-commit only (internal/git/git.go:63).
- Comments anchor on path+line only; store.Comment.BlobSHA exists but the frontend never sends it (CommentInput is {path,side,line,body}), so blob_sha is always empty.
- Reviews are keyed by (branch, base) in EnsureReview (store.go:96); that key flows into persistence, the agent prompt, and the WebSocket.
- Direct mode already edits the working tree (adapter.go:45).
- Layout is a 2-col grid: .layout { grid-template-columns: 1fr 360px } (diff + right sidebar, styles.css:44). File <section>s have no scroll-target id yet. files: FileDiff[] (each with .path) is already in App state.
- Vitest + go test harness now exist (make test) — new pure modules and git_test.go are testable.

title: Review uncommitted/working-tree changes
description:
Let loupe review the working tree (committed + uncommitted changes), not just committed branch diffs. Treat the working tree as a selectable pseudo-branch via a sentinel value (e.g. git.WorkingRef = '*working*') so it reuses the existing base/branch UI, (branch,base) persistence key, prompt path, and WebSocket with minimal new surface.

## Backend
1. internal/git/git.go — add DiffWorking(base string) (string, error): mb := merge-base(base, HEAD); 'git diff --no-color <mb>' (working tree vs base — committed + uncommitted together; subsumes 'git diff HEAD' when base is the current branch tip, so uncommitted edits on main work too). Untracked files do NOT appear in plain 'git diff' — either enumerate 'git ls-files --others --exclude-standard' and 'git diff --no-index /dev/null <file>' per file, or document untracked as out of scope for v1.
2. internal/server/server.go — define one shared sentinel const; in handleDiff, when branch == sentinel call DiffWorking(base); apply the same dispatch in runReview (server.go:248) where it currently calls s.git.Diff.
3. internal/adapter/adapter.go — special-case the prompt header wording when branch is the sentinel ('reviewing uncommitted changes against base').

## Frontend
4. web/src/App.tsx — add a 'Working tree (uncommitted)' option at the top of the branch dropdown mapping to the sentinel. No API shape changes; ensureReview/submitReview/persistence key off the sentinel string transparently.
5. Add a 'Refresh diff' button — working-tree diffs are live, but the current effect only refetches on base/branch change.

## Trade-offs
- Anchor drift: as you edit, line numbers shift and stored comments can land on the wrong line. Acceptable for v1 (same model as today); future fix is content-based anchoring instead of raw line number.
- Sentinel collision with a real branch literally named '*working*' is vanishingly unlikely; alternative is a dedicated ?working=1 param, but persistence still needs a synthetic branch key, so the sentinel is less code.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting 'Working tree (uncommitted)' as the branch shows a diff of committed + uncommitted changes vs the base; comments can be added, persist, and submit to the agent on that view; runReview uses the working-tree diff for the prompt; a Refresh button re-pulls the live diff. internal/git/git_test.go covers DiffWorking (base commit + committed change + uncommitted edit + untracked file) and a server test confirms the sentinel routes to the working-tree diff. 'go test ./...' passes.
notes: Resolves the question from the prior session: loupe currently only diffs committed state.

comments.author: coordinator
comments.text:
Implementation complete: Implemented "Review uncommitted/working-tree changes" (loupe-2sq.1).

BACKEND:

- internal/server/server.go: added diffFor(base,branch) that dispatches the sentinel to DiffWorking; wired into BOTH handleDiff and runReview (so the live view and the agent prompt use the same diff).
- internal/adapter/adapter.go: BuildPrompt special-cases the sentinel with "reviewing uncommitted changes against base" header wording.

FRONTEND (web/src/App.tsx):
- Added "Working tree (uncommitted)" option at the top of the branch dropdown mapping to the sentinel; ensureReview/submitReview/persistence key off the sentinel string with no API shape changes.
- Added a "Refresh diff" button; split the diff fetch into its own effect (keyed on base/branch/refreshKey) so live working-tree diffs re-pull without resetting comment state.

TESTS:
- internal/git/git_test.go (new): DiffWorking covers base commit + committed change + uncommitted edit + untracked file, plus a test confirming it diverges from the committed-only Diff.
- internal/server/server_test.go: TestDiffWorkingRefRoutesToWorkingTree spins up a real git repo and confirms /api/diff?branch=*working* surfaces an uncommitted edit the committed diff does not.

- Runtime smoke test (built binary on :7878 + agent-browser): selected "Working tree (uncommitted)" → 8 file sections rendered, console clean, no WebSocket errors; Refresh button works; added a comment that persisted under branch="*working*" (verified via /api/reviews), then cleaned it up. title: Collapsible file-tree sidebar (left) for changeset navigation
description:
Add a left panel that turns the flat file list into a navigable, collapsible tree; clicking a file scrolls the diff to it. The panel itself can also collapse to a thin rail.

## New pure module — web/src/filetree.ts (unit-testable)
- buildTree(paths: string[]): TreeNode[] — fold 'a/b/c.go' paths into nested dir/file nodes, dirs-first + alphabetical. This is the only piece with real logic; gets filetree.test.ts (Vitest harness already exists).

## New component — web/src/FileTree.tsx
- Recursive render; directory nodes collapsible (local useState<Set<string>> of collapsed dirs, or native <details>); file nodes call onSelect(path).
- Optional per-file badges: pending-comment count (from existing comments state — high value for review nav) and +/- line counts (computable from FileDiff.hunks).

## App.tsx wiring
- Give each file <section> a stable id (fileId(path)); add scrollToFile(path) reusing the existing jumpTo smooth-scroll + flash pattern.
- Add sidebarCollapsed state + a toggle (header button or rail chevron). Pass files, comment counts, and active path to <FileTree>.
- Optional scroll-spy (IntersectionObserver) to highlight the file currently in view.

## styles.css
- Change .layout to grid-template-columns: <tree> 1fr 360px; collapsed state shrinks the tree column to a narrow rail (~28px) with just an expand chevron.
- Add .filetree panel, indentation, dir/file rows, hover/active highlight, long-name truncation — using existing --panel/--border/--accent/--muted tokens to match the theme.
acceptance_criteria: A left sidebar shows the changeset as a collapsible directory tree; clicking a file scrolls the diff to that file's section (with the existing flash). Directories expand/collapse and the whole panel collapses to a rail. buildTree is covered by web/src/filetree.test.ts and 'make test' passes. Empty changeset, deep nesting, and many-file cases render sanely.
notes: files: FileDiff[] is already in App state, so no new data fetching is needed.

title: Context-aware comment anchoring to mitigate line drift
description:
Comments currently anchor on (path, line) only — store.Comment.BlobSHA exists but is never populated (the frontend CommentInput sends just {path,side,line,body}, and App.tsx renders comments by matching c.path===f.path && c.line===ln). When the underlying diff shifts (working-tree edits, or amend/rebase of a committed branch), a comment's stored line points at the wrong content or vanishes from view. This adds a content anchor so drifted comments relocate instead of silently misplacing.

Scope here is the MINIMAL v1; robust version noted as follow-on.

## v1 (this issue)
### Capture (cheap — most of it already exists)
- store.go: add an 'anchor_text' column via the existing migrations mechanism (the ALTER TABLE … 'duplicate column name'-tolerant list). Trivial; pattern is already there.
- web/src/api.ts: widen CommentInput with the captured line text. The content is already in hand at capture time — openNew(path, line: DiffLine) holds line.content; stash it in the editor target so saveEditor can send it.
- handleAddComment already decodes into store.Comment, so the field flows through with no handler change once the struct has it.

### Relocation (the real logic — pure + unit-tested)
- A pure helper (e.g. web/src/anchor.ts): given a stored anchor (anchor_text + original line) and the freshly parsed FileDiff, return the best current line. Heuristic: verify the line at the stored number still matches anchor_text; else search outward ±N lines for an exact content match; else flag the comment orphaned.
- Unit-test under the existing Vitest harness — cover the shifted-line, duplicate-line, and deleted-line cases.

### Orphaned-comment UI
- Today comments only render inline at a matched (path, line); an unrelocatable comment currently just disappears. Add a simple per-file collapsed 'outdated comments' section so orphans have a home.

## Follow-on (NOT this issue — file separately if pursued)
- Context window (context_before/after lines) for more robust matching when a line's text is duplicated.
- Populate + use blob_sha as a fast path: file unchanged since the comment → trust the stored line as-is, skip relocation.
- Properly tuned fuzzy matcher.

## Notes
- Independent of the working-tree feature (loupe-2sq.1): also fixes drift on amend/rebase of a committed branch. Natural companion, not a dependency.
acceptance_criteria: An 'anchor_text' column captures the commented line's content at creation. On render, a comment whose stored line no longer matches relocates to the nearest line with matching content (searched within a ±N window); a comment that can't be relocated appears in a per-file 'outdated comments' section instead of vanishing. A pure relocation helper is covered by tests (shifted-line, duplicate-line, deleted-line cases) and 'make test' passes.
notes: Effort estimate: ~0.5 day for this v1; ~1.5–2 days for the robust follow-on. Capture is nearly free (BlobSHA column + migration pattern already exist, frontend already holds line.content); the relocation function and orphaned-comment UI are the actual work.

title: Fold working changes into the current-branch view (no separate selection)
description:
Refinement of loupe-2sq.1. When the selected branch IS the currently checked-out branch, the diff should automatically include uncommitted working changes — the user should not have to pick the separate '*working*' (Working tree) option to see their in-progress work against base.

## Behavior
- If branch == git.CurrentBranch(): show 'git diff <merge-base(base, HEAD)>' (committed + uncommitted together) — i.e. route to the same DiffWorking path 2sq.1 adds.
- If branch is any OTHER (non-checked-out) branch: keep the commit-to-commit diff (you can't show a working tree for a branch that isn't checked out).
- The branch picker already defaults to the current branch (App.tsx useEffect on getBranches), so the default view becomes 'my current work including uncommitted changes' with no extra clicks.

## Implementation
- internal/server/server.go: diffFor already centralizes the dispatch (it currently routes the git.WorkingRef sentinel to DiffWorking). Extend it: also route to DiffWorking(base) when branch == s.git.CurrentBranch(). runReview already shares diffFor, so the agent prompt stays consistent with the live view.
- No new frontend selection needed. Optionally drop or de-emphasize the explicit '*working*' option if this makes it redundant for the common case (see open question).

## Open questions / decisions
- Does this SUPERSEDE the explicit WorkingRef sentinel from 2sq.1? The sentinel is still useful for reviewing the working tree against an arbitrary base, or uncommitted edits while on the base branch itself — but folding working changes into the current-branch view may make the separate dropdown entry unnecessary for most users. Decide whether to keep the sentinel as an advanced option or remove it.
- Consider a 'committed only' toggle, since with this change the current-branch view no longer shows the pure committed diff.

## Caveats
- Makes the current-branch view live (changes as you edit), so the anchor-drift concern in loupe-2sq.3 now applies to the default view, not just the opt-in working-tree view.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting (or defaulting to) the currently checked-out branch shows a diff that includes uncommitted working changes against base, without choosing a separate option. Non-checked-out branches still show the committed-only diff. diffFor and runReview agree on the diff. Covered by a server test (current branch includes an uncommitted edit; a different branch does not). 'go test ./...' passes.
notes: Discovered while planning 2sq.1; depends on its DiffWorking/diffFor machinery.

title: Harden review-persistence API: r.ok checks, tx for MarkSubmitted, id parse errors
description:
Follow-ups from the loupe-1mf.1 persistence work (commits 81e280f, fd3bea1), intentionally kept out of that approved diff. The repo currently has ZERO tests, so this ticket also bootstraps a test suite — the fixes below should land with coverage.

Stack: Go 1.23 backend (internal/), React+Vite frontend (web/), single binary via `make build`. Manual validation: drive the running app with `agent-browser` against /tmp/loupe-test (a repo with `main` vs `feat/multiply`).

## 1. Frontend: check r.ok in all fetch helpers
File: web/src/api.ts (helpers ~lines 38–93). Each does `await fetch(...)` then reads the body without checking status. Concrete failures:
- submitReview swallows a 400 "no pending comments to submit"; the UI proceeds as if it worked.
- ensureReview returns undefined on error, which then builds a WebSocket URL `/api/reviews/undefined/ws`.
Fix: a shared guard, e.g.
    async function json<T>(r: Response): Promise<T> {
      if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${r.status} ${await r.text()}`)
      return r.json() as Promise<T>
    }
Route every helper through it (plus a no-body variant for the 204 cases: updateComment, deleteComment, submitReview). Surface thrown errors in the submit/agent flow in web/src/App.tsx instead of failing silently.
AC: every api.ts helper rejects on non-2xx with the response text; a 400 from submit shows a visible error and does NOT open a WebSocket; no request is ever made to /api/reviews/undefined/...

## 2. Backend: transactional MarkSubmitted
File: internal/store/store.go, MarkSubmitted. It runs pendingComments() (SELECT) then a separate UPDATE. A comment inserted between the two gets flagged submitted=1, collapsed=1 by the UPDATE but is absent from the returned batch — so it's marked submitted yet never sent to the agent (silently dropped).
Fix: run SELECT + UPDATE in one *sql.Tx (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), or switch to a single `UPDATE comments SET submitted=1, collapsed=1 WHERE review_id=? AND submitted=0 RETURNING <all cols>` (SQLite >=3.35; modernc.org/sqlite supports RETURNING) so the flagged rows and the returned batch are provably identical.
AC: the comments returned by MarkSubmitted are exactly the rows it flagged; a regression test covering the insert-during-submit interleaving passes.

## 3. Backend: reject non-numeric path ids
File: internal/server/server.go — six sites of `id, _ := strconv.ParseInt(chi.URLParam(r, "id"), 10, 64)` (~lines 137, 147, 171, 199, 214, 270). The discarded error makes a bad id become 0 and hit the store as a silent miss. Add a helper:
    func pathID(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (int64, bool) {
      id, err := strconv.ParseInt(chi.URLParam(r, "id"), 10, 64)
      if err != nil { http.Error(w, "invalid id", http.StatusBadRequest); return 0, false }
      return id, true
    }
Use it at all six sites (early-return on !ok).
AC: GET /api/reviews/abc/comments (and the other id routes) returns 400, not 200/500-with-id-0.

## 4. Decide on the unused GET /api/reviews/{id}/comments
Registered (handleListComments) but has no SPA caller — listReviews already embeds comments. Either remove the route+handler, or keep it with a one-line comment marking it intentional API surface.
AC: the route is either gone or documented as deliberate.

## Initialize a test suite
No tests exist. Bootstrap one so the fixes above land verified and future work has a harness. Go is the priority; frontend tests are a stretch goal.

### Go (primary)
`go test ./...` works with the stdlib — no deps to add. Add a Makefile target:
    test:
    	go test ./...
    	cd web && npm test --silent --if-present
Tests to write (table-driven where natural):
- internal/store/store_test.go — open a throwaway DB via Open(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "t.db")) (modernc sqlite is cgo-free, runs anywhere). Cover: EnsureReview get-or-create idempotency; AddComment returns a usable id; MarkSubmitted returns exactly the flagged rows (the item-2 regression); UpdateComment / DeleteComment / Comments / Reviews filtering. Highest-value coverage — it's the persistence layer the feature rests on.
- internal/server/server_test.go — build the router with server.New(...) and exercise it via net/http/httptest (httptest.NewRecorder + srv.ServeHTTP). Cover comment CRUD + reviews endpoints and the item-3 400 cases. The submit endpoint spawns claude, so test only its pre-spawn behavior (empty-pending -> 400, which returns before `go runReview`). To test submit's success path without a real agent, extract the agent runner behind a small interface and inject a no-op — note as an OPTIONAL refactor, not required here.
- internal/git/git_test.go (optional) — create a temp repo with git init + two branches; assert Branches() / MergeBase() / Diff(). Integration-flavored; fine to skip.

### Frontend (stretch)
No runner configured. Add Vitest (npm i -D vitest), a "test": "vitest run" script, and:
- web/src/diff.test.ts — parseUnifiedDiff is pure and the easiest high-value target (feed a known git diff, assert files/hunks/line kinds + line numbers).
- The duplicate-`result` dedup logic (loupe-1mf.2) currently lives inline in App.tsx's ws.onmessage. Extract it into a pure helper (e.g. web/src/events.ts) and unit-test it — covers the bugfix and removes DOM coupling. React component tests (Testing Library) are out of scope.

### CI (optional)
A minimal .github/workflows/ci.yml running `go test ./...` + `npm ci && npm test` would lock this in, but isn't required to close the ticket.
acceptance_criteria: All four items fixed: (1) every web/src/api.ts helper rejects on non-2xx and the UI surfaces it (never requests /api/reviews/undefined/...); (2) MarkSubmitted is atomic — the returned batch equals exactly the rows it flagged, with a regression test for the insert-during-submit interleaving; (3) all six path-id routes in server.go return 400 on a non-numeric id; (4) the unused GET /api/reviews/{id}/comments route is removed or documented as intentional. A Go test suite exists and 'go test ./...' passes, including store_test.go (EnsureReview idempotency + the MarkSubmitted regression) and server_test.go (the id-400 cases), wired into a 'make test' target. Previously-approved persistence still works (spot-checked via agent-browser).
